findings.reason: The protected app-local and Accepted native sources implement concise increasing-choice backtracking over digits 1 through 9. They prevent reuse and permutation duplicates by advancing the next candidate, stop once candidates exceed the remaining sum, and copy only exact length-k zero-remainder paths. The fixed domain makes stronger pruning a non-material optimization, so no candidate is justified.

The former benchmark used synthetic 8/64/256 search units and included k = 1 outside the source contract. Scaling cannot be honest because every input searches the same fixed nine-digit universe. A verified bounded-domain certificate now proves at most 2^9 subset states, O(2^9 k) time including output copies, and O(k) auxiliary path depth.

The approach formerly attributed available-slot and minimum/maximum achievable-sum pruning to sources that implement none of those checks. It now describes the exact increasing recursion and value-greater-than-remaining break, moves stronger bounds to alternatives, and states a safe whole-search complexity bound.
